messages:
carmen: Hey folks — got married abroad last month and trying to add my spouse. Marriage cert from the local municipality is digital but no apostille yet. Do we have guidance for international docs and retro coverage?

maya-hr: Congrats! :tada: Quick answers: we can accept embassy/consulate-certified marriage records OR the original foreign certificate plus a certified translation. If apostille is delayed, consular stamp + booking reference helps.

carmen: thanks — is there a window to submit? I missed the 30-day QLE window because of the paperwork backlog.

maya-hr: Fair point. Our policy: standard QLE window is 30 days, but for documented international processing delays we allow up to 60 days to submit supporting docs. If docs are submitted within 90 days we can do retro coverage to the marriage date on a case-by-case basis — requires manager + HR signoff.

carmen: great. What about payroll proration and when premiums will start?

leo-payroll: We handle premiums effective date based on the coverage start we set in benefits. If we set coverage retro to the marriage date, payroll will retro-adjust deductions and either a small positive or negative balancing item will appear on the next paycheck. Typical timeline: adjustments applied in the next payroll cycle after HR finalizes enrollment (1–2 pay periods).

carmen: ok noted. How do I upload the docs? Is email ok or should I use the portal?

maya-hr: Please use the benefits portal (preferred) so docs are attached to your case. Portal path: 

```
Benefits Portal -> My Open Requests -> Add Dependent -> Upload Documents
```
If you must email, send to benefits@redwood.ai with subject: "QLE docs - Carmen" and we’ll move them into the portal.

carmen: attached a PDF from the municipality but it’s only in Spanish. Will that be okay if I include a notarized English translation from a local translator?

maya-hr: Yes — certified translation accepted. If notarization is not available locally, a translation from a recognized translation service plus the consular stamp should work. Include any booking/appointment confirmations showing you attempted to get apostille to strengthen the case.

carmen: Perfect. I’ll upload tonight. Any special note I should add on the portal request?

maya-hr: Add a short note: "Marriage abroad - delayed apostille; submitting consular-stamped certificate + certified translation; requesting retro coverage to [marriage date]." That helps routing.

carmen: Thanks!

hr-bot: Ticket #PO-2024-1789 created and assigned to maya-hr. Upload link sent to Carmen by DM.

tom-manager: +1 from me for retro start if docs look valid. Happy to sign off once maya confirms.

maya-hr: Thanks Tom, appreciate the quick review. Carmen — once you upload I’ll mark docs as received and loop payroll. Expect an email confirmation from us within 3 business days after upload. :thumbsup:
